1. HOW TO “PLAY” A CARD

Unless otherwise specified on a card, or depending on the type of card, a player can only play cards or activate effects during their turn during the Summon Phase.

Play is a broad term that encompasses using Unit or Leader effects, activating Spells or Enchantments, and Summoning, Calling, or Evolving cards.

Cards and effects may have additional requirements or exceptions that allow them to be used outside of these standard rules.

QUICK

If a card has a lightning bolt symbol at the beginning of its effect text, preceding the Cost, that effect is able to be chained and used on either turn, so long as the remainder of the Trigger requirements are met.

LEADER

There are exceptions, but the way a Leader will be “played” nearly every time is through an Evolution, specifically a Leader Evolution.

To perform a Leader Evolution, first check the Leader card you are attempting to Evolve into. Then check the board for a valid target that you control.

A valid target is a Leader in your Active Leader Zone that:
- Is 1 level lower than the attempted Evolution.
- Shares at least 1 Essence Attribute with the attempted Evolution.
- Shares at least 1 Keyword with the attempted Evolution.

If these conditions are met, verify that you have the required amount of Mana.

The amount of Mana required for a Leader Evolution is the Mana Cost of the attempted Evolution minus the Mana Cost of the Leader currently in play, to a minimum of 0.

The player then:
1. Taps that amount of Mana.
2. Removes the Active Leader from play.
3. Evolution Summons the new Leader.

Unless otherwise specified, the new Leader comes into play untapped.

UNIT

There are 3 different ways that a Unit may be “played”:
- Summon
- Call
- Evolve

All of these are subject to change due to card effects.

The Level of a Unit must be equal to or less than the Level of your current Active Leader for it to be played.

There are 6 Active Unit Zones.

If there are no available Active Unit Zones, you must send any 1 Active Unit of your choice to the Grave after paying any Mana Cost, if required, before the Unit can be played.

For all three methods, the player must control the cards they are attempting to use and can only Summon to their own board unless otherwise specified.

SUMMON

For a Summon, a player taps Mana equal to the Mana Cost of the card in order to place that Unit as Active on the board in one of the 6 Active Unit Zones.

For a Summon, the Unit comes in untapped unless otherwise specified.

CALL

For a Call, a player does not pay the Mana Cost of a Unit to play it as Active on the board in one of the 6 Active Unit Zones.

For a Call, the Unit comes in untapped unless otherwise specified.

EVOLVE

For an Evolve, first check the Level, Essence Attribute(s), and Keyword(s) of the card being attempted.

Then check the Level, Essence Attribute(s), and Keyword(s) of the on-board Unit being attempted to Evolve over.

The on-board Unit is a valid target if it:
- Is 1 level lower than the Unit attempting to Evolve over it.
- Shares at least 1 Essence Attribute with it.
- Shares at least 1 Keyword with it.

The player then taps Mana equal to the Mana Cost of the Unit in hand minus the Mana Cost of the Unit on board, to a minimum of 0.

The on-board Unit is then sent to the Grave and the Unit in hand is Evolution Summoned.

That Unit comes in untapped unless otherwise specified.

If the Unit being Evolved over has an Enchantment equipped to it, that Enchantment is equipped to the new Unit. This is not considered targeting the new Unit.

The Unit being sent to the Grave and the new Unit being Evolution Summoned occur at the same time for trigger purposes. Therefore, effects such as “(When this Unit Evolution Summons)” and “(When this Unit is Evolved over)” can both successfully trigger. The player who performed the Evolution chooses the order in which those triggers resolve.

SPELL

There are 3 types of Spells, signified by the Keyword of the Spell card.

The Keyword of a Spell determines when that card is able to be used from the hand.

Some Spell cards may have additional effects with a Trigger, allowing for additional restrictions or allowing them to be used from places other than the hand.

For any Spell to be used from hand, its Level must be equal to or lower than the Level of your Active Leader, unless otherwise specified.

For any Spell to be used from hand, the player must also tap Mana equal to the Spell’s Mana Cost, unless otherwise specified.

When a Spell card resolves its effect, it is sent to the Grave.

CHANNELED

A Channeled Spell can only be used from your hand during your turn, during your Summon Phase, unless otherwise specified.

This type of Spell cannot be chained to other effects or actions.

COUNTERSPELL

A Counterspell can be used from your hand during either player’s turn and can be chained to other effects or actions.

OVER SPELL

An Overspell can be used from your hand during either player’s turn and can be chained to other effects or actions.

No effects can be chained to an Overspell.

ENCHANTMENT

There are 2 types of Enchantments, signified by the Keyword of the Enchantment card.

Enchantments can only be used from your hand during your turn, during your Summon Phase.

An Enchantment is played by tapping Mana equal to its Mana Cost, then targeting a Unit on either board and placing the Enchantment under that Unit, equipping it.

Only 1 Enchantment may be placed below a Unit at a time.

If a Unit would Evolve over another Unit that has an Enchantment, that Enchantment is equipped to the new Unit. This is not considered targeting the new Unit.

When an Enchantment would be used on a Unit that already has an Enchantment under it, send the previous Enchantment to the Grave.

When a Unit leaves the board, other than by being used as Evolve material, the Enchantment is sent to the Grave.

3. THE ANATOMY OF A CARD

The anatomy of a card is important to understanding how cards work and interact with each other, and is vital for deck construction.

Understanding the different sections of a card will allow you to determine what a card is, what it can do, and how it interacts with other cards.

TYPE

A card’s Type is not displayed in a specific section. Instead, it is determined by the context of the card.

If a card has gold encasement for its Level as well as a Mana Value section, it is a Leader card.

If it has silver encasement as well as a Mana Value section, it is a Unit card.

Gold encasement with no Mana Value section is an Enchantment.

Silver encasement with no Mana Value section is a Spell.

While this may seem confusing when described in text, the Type of a card should be visually apparent when viewing the cards themselves.

LEVEL

A card’s Level can be found in the upper-left corner of a card, inside of a gold or silver circle that appears somewhat like a sun, with small prongs in a “+” formation.

A card’s Level determines when that card is able to be played.

There are ways to modify what Level a card may be treated as, allowing it to be played outside of the normal requirements of its printed Level.

There are also cards and effects that may ignore Level requirements to “cheat out” a card.

A card’s Level must be equal to or lower than the Level of your Active Leader to be played.

MANA COST

A card’s Mana Cost can be found in the upper-right corner of a card, inside of a gold or silver circle with small prongs in an “X” formation.

To play a card, you must tap an amount of Mana cards in your Mana Pool equal to its Mana Cost.

There are ways to modify the amount of Mana that must be paid for a card to be played. There are also various situations where a card might be played without paying any Cost to “cheat out” a card.

MANA VALUE

A card’s Mana Value can be found below the Level of a card and appears as a number of blue gemstones inside of gold or silver clasps.

If a card does not have this section, that card is either a Spell or Enchantment.

If a card does have this section, that card is either a Unit or Leader.

The amount of blue gemstones on a Unit or Leader varies between 1–5. The number of blue gemstones determines how many Mana cards that card “untaps” when it “channels.”

A card can “channel” while it is in play and its controller chooses to “tap-to-channel” that card during the Summon Phase of their turn.

When this is performed, the controller untaps a number of Mana cards equal to that card’s Mana Value.

NAME

A card’s name can be found between the Level and Mana Cost sections at the top of a card.

There are various effects that may target or search for a card based on the characters found in its name, including names displayed within quotation marks.

PICTURE

A card’s picture can be found in the top half of the card, in the center, and displays a graphic that is meant to represent the card.

KEYWORDS

A card’s Keywords can be found in the bottom-left corner of its picture.

A Unit or Leader can have up to 5 Keywords.

A Spell or Enchantment will only have 1 Keyword.

Each Keyword is separated by a “/”.

There are various effects that may target or search for a card based on its Keywords. Keywords referenced within card effects are displayed in italics.

EFFECT

A card’s Effect or Effects can be found in the bottom half of the card, in the center. This text box contains lines of text that describe the effects a card performs.

While the structure of a card effect may seem complex at first, it is designed to leave little room for interpretation about when an effect can be used and what it does.

More information about how to read and understand card effects can be found in The Anatomy Of An Effect.

ESSENCE ATTRIBUTE

Sometimes shortened to Essence, a card’s Essence Attribute can be found in the bottom-left corner of a card, inside of gold or silver circles.

Each symbol in one of these circles shows which Essence Attributes that card has.

Essence Attributes are found in card text as white text over a large black banner.

Essence Attributes are important for deck construction, as any Unit card must share at least 1 Essence Attribute with your Starting Leader.

Your Starting Leader is a Level 0 Leader card that is played at the beginning of a Duel.

BATTLE POWER

A card’s Battle Power, or BP, can be found in the bottom-right corner of a card.

This value determines how cards interact with each other during Combat.

An attacking Unit or Leader with a higher or equal BP compared to a defending Unit destroys that defending Unit.

LIMIT SYMBOL

A card may or may not have a small black star in the upper-right corner of the card, just above the Mana Cost section.

If a card has this symbol, only 1 copy of that card’s name may be used in a Deck.


4. THE ANATOMY OF AN EFFECT

Understanding the structure of an effect is important for determining when an effect can be used, what requirements must be met, what Cost must be paid, and what happens when the effect resolves.

DESCRIPTORS

Text in italics at the top of a card that is outside of an effect’s Trigger Condition is a descriptor for restrictions or exceptions that cause a card to be played outside of the norm.

This portion is not considered an effect.

EFFECTS WITHOUT TRIGGER CONDITIONS

If a card has text that is not in italics but has no Trigger Condition specified, that effect does not have requirements for events in which it can be used other than the standard game rules.

TRIGGER CONDITIONS

A card’s Trigger Condition is displayed in small bold text above the effect that would be activated when the Trigger Condition is met.

A Trigger Condition can be broken down into a “Where, Why, When” format and requires that all 3 conditions are met, in that order.

WHERE

The Where is the location the card must be in.

It is found within brackets, such as [Board] or [Hand].

WHY

The Why is the situation that must occur for the card’s effect to activate.

It is found within parentheses, such as (When this Unit is Summoned) or (When a player draws a card).

WHEN

The When determines when the effect is allowed to be used.

It is found between hyphens, such as -During your turn- or -Auto-.

The When portion is particularly important because different When conditions have different rules.

CONTINUOUS

-Continuous- is a non-triggering effect that simply remains active as long as its conditions are met.

Continuous effects do not trigger Chains.

AUTO

-Auto- is a Trigger that automatically triggers without giving either player a decision.

ONCE

-Once- means that the effect can only be used a single time by that card while it remains in its Trigger location.

ONCE PER TURN

-Once per turn- means that the effect can be used again on the following turn.

Other timing conditions, including -Once, during either player’s turn- and -Once per either player’s turn-, have their own specific timing restrictions.

Certain cards can be chained to each other when conditions allow.

A Chain occurs when a second card, effect, or action is activated in response to an existing action or effect, such as Summoning, Evolving, using a Unit effect, using a Spell or Enchantment, Attacking, Defending, or other actions or effects that allow a response.

For more information about Chains, see Chains And Priority.

COST AND EFFECT

The Cost to be paid for a card effect is found in the card’s effect text, before the arrow.

The Effect of the card is found in the card’s effect text, after the arrow.

Negating a card’s effect does not prevent the effect from triggering or its Cost from being paid. Instead, negating the effect prevents the Effect after the arrow from resolving.

6. DECK CONSTRUCTION

A Deck is comprised of 3 main parts:
- The Leader Deck
- The Mana Deck
- The Main Deck

The limit for the number of copies of a card with the same name is 3, unless that card has a black star in the upper-right corner.

Cards with a black star are limited to 1 copy.

LEADER DECK

The Leader Deck is made up of exactly 6 Leader cards.

Leader cards are a type of card that has 3 Essence Attribute slots at the bottom-left corner.

A Leader Deck must contain exactly 1 copy of exactly 1 Level 0 Leader card.

The remainder of the Leader Deck may contain any other Leader cards, provided they do not exceed the game’s copy limit.

Standard Leader Decks will usually contain Leader cards of Levels 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5.

The Level 0 Leader is placed on the board as the player’s Active Leader at the beginning of the Duel.

The remaining Leaders in the Leader Deck are generally used to Evolve the Active Leader, increasing its Level and therefore increasing the Levels of cards the player is able to play.

MANA DECK

The Mana Deck is made up of exactly 10 Mana cards.

Mana cards are used to visually display the total amount of Mana a player has available per turn and to keep track of how much Mana has already been “spent” or “tapped” and how much is “available” or “untapped.”

MAIN DECK

The Main Deck is made up of exactly 50 cards.

Any combination of Units, Spells, and Enchantments may be used to reach the total of 50 cards.

The Units that can be included in a Deck are determined by the Essence Attributes of the Level 0 Leader in the Deck and the Essence Attributes of the Units being added.

All Units in a Main Deck must share at least 1 Essence Attribute with the Level 0 Leader.
